---
title: Displays and local dashboard
---

## Notebook and terminal

`progress=True` selects an anywidget notebook display when available, otherwise a Rich terminal display. Both show sampler phases, per-chain progress, variable-wise worst R-hat and ESS, and the controller's checks and verdict. Install `[notebook]` for notebook rendering. Notebook stop messages use the widget comm channel and a shared `RunControl`; frontend responsiveness depends on the host notebook's comm scheduling. For independent cancellation during a blocking cell, use the localhost dashboard or `start()`.

## Authenticated localhost

```python
handle = monitor.start(model=model, dashboard=True, progress=False)
print(handle.dashboard_url)
try:
    idata = handle.wait()
    # The dashboard remains readable until close().
finally:
    handle.close()
```

Install the `dashboard` extra first. `Dashboard(*, port=0, title="pymc-monitor", idle_timeout=300)` binds a preallocated socket on `127.0.0.1`. A per-instance token in the initial navigation path grants an HttpOnly SameSite cookie; the browser then removes the token from its history and reloads through a cookie-only URL. Treat the original URL as a credential. Non-browser API clients can send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Never put a token in query strings or expose this port publicly.

Every route requires authentication and validates Host and Origin. Stop is POST-only; unknown runs return 404, and finished or already-stopping runs return 409. The service does not enable cross-origin requests. Its HTML contains all its CSS and JavaScript (including vendored uPlot), with a hash-based Content Security Policy and no third-party scripts or analytics. All run-supplied names, errors and hints render as text, not executable HTML. Trace previews show at most 20 elements and 500 points per chain. They are diagnostic previews, not a replacement for posterior plots.

The server is local to the Python host. A notebook running remotely does not make that machine's loopback URL accessible on your laptop. Do not expose the server publicly or publish its token. Remote transport belongs in a separate application.

## Reusable presentation

A shared `Dashboard()` can serve several `start(..., dashboard=dashboard)` handles; each has an isolated run URL and stop control. `overview_url()` opens a token-free-cookie-redirected overview; authenticated `GET /progress` returns the shared `{models, runs}` manifest, and `POST /stop` stops active runs, or one run with `?model=<label>`. Removing one handle retains the others, and the idle server shuts down after `idle_timeout` seconds with no runs. Close the shared instance explicitly when done.

`DashboardState(completion_phase="sampling")` is a lock-protected, transport-independent event reducer with `update(event)`, `show_phase`, `show_sampling`, `show_convergence`, `request_stop`, `finish(status)`, and `snapshot()`. Use `completion_phase="downloading"` to keep a cloud dashboard open after sampling ends; a `RunFinished` sampling verdict does not mark downloading complete. Snapshots are independent JSON-safe copies. `render_dashboard_html(*, progress_url, stop_url, token, title="pymc-monitor")` returns self-contained HTML with escaped JSON configuration and supports flat states or `{models: [{label, name}], runs: {label: state}}`. `dashboard_csp(*, progress_url, stop_url=None)` hashes the inline assets and restricts connections to validated API origins. A null stop URL hides controls. For remote hosts, serve the HTML with the returned CSP and allow CORS for the page's origin at the explicit API endpoints; progress and stop requests pass nonempty tokens in query parameters without custom headers or bodies. `dashboard_assets()` returns the bundled source assets.

A consuming application owns authentication and transport. It can dispatch typed events to the reducer and serve these assets without importing any cloud dependency into pymc-monitor. The local HTTP service is only one adapter for that state.
